intro.title: Utility Types
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple user profile component that displays and manages user data. You will learn how to use TypeScript's utility types, such as Partial and Pick, to make your types more flexible and reusable. The main technologies involved are React with TypeScript (TSX) and TypeScript's type system. By the end, you'll understand how utility types help you create new types from existing ones, reducing code duplication and improving type safety in your React applications.
intro.usecase: Utility Types are essential in real-world React applications where you need to transform or constrain data types without rewriting them. For example, when building a user dashboard that displays partial user profiles, you'd use `Partial<User>` to safely handle incomplete data. In complex forms with validation, `Pick` and `Omit` help create strict type definitions for form fields while excluding sensitive data like passwords. These types ensure type safety when filtering data tables, managing API responses, or creating reusable component props across your application.
